findings.evidence: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/WeightedRestrictedSeries.lean:994` defines `weightedRestrictedSubring_ringHom_ext_of_continuous` under only `[Semiring B] [TopologicalSpace B] [T2Space B]`; `WeightedEval/UniversalProperty.lean:80` uses it rather than reproving it inside the `∃!`. `Mathlib/Topology/UniformSpace/Completion.lean:414` shows `Completion.ext` needs only `[T2Space Y]`. The PR description names `A⟨X⟩⟨Y⟩ ≅ A⟨X,Y⟩` as the next consumer, which needs ext, not `∃!.unique` (using `.unique` forces re-deriving continuity and both value clauses for each of the two maps).
findings.fix: Extract `completion_weightedRestrictedSubring_ringHom_ext_of_continuous {f g : Completion (weightedRestrictedSubring T hT) →+* B} (hf : Continuous f) (hg : Continuous g) (hC : ∀ a, f ↑(weightedC T hT a) = g ↑(weightedC T hT a)) (hX : ∀ i, f ↑(weightedX T hT i) = g ↑(weightedX T hT i)) : f = g`, proved by `weightedRestrictedSubring_ringHom_ext_of_continuous` on the restrictions along `coeRingHom` followed by `Completion.ext`, then make the `∃!` uniqueness clause a one-line application of it. This mirrors how the uncompleted file is organised.
findings.issue: The extensionality content (`two continuous ring homs out of Completion (weightedRestrictedSubring T hT) agreeing on `↑(weightedC ·)` and `↑(weightedX ·)` are equal`) is inlined in the `∃!` proof, so it is unavailable to consumers. It is also strictly more general than the form it is used at here: the argument needs neither `φ`, `hφ`, `hb`, `CompleteSpace B` nor `T3Space B`, only `[Semiring B] [TopologicalSpace B] [T2Space B]`.

findings.evidence: `Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/UniformRing.lean:115` defines `coeRingHom` with `toFun := (↑)` and has no `coeRingHom_apply` lemma (grep for `coeRingHom_apply` in ./mathlib matches only `Mathlib/Order/Filter/Germ/Basic.lean:605`); `Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Hom/Defs.lean:551` is `RingHom.coe_comp`, and `Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/UniformRing.lean:122` is `continuous_coeRingHom`, already used in this repo at `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/Completion.lean:455`.
findings.fix: Use `Completion.continuous_coeRingHom` in place of `Completion.continuous_coe _`, insert an explicit `simp only [RingHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply]` (or `RingHom.comp_apply` rewrites) where the composed hom's application is needed, and — since Mathlib has no `coeRingHom_apply` lemma — add a one-line comment stating that `⇑Completion.coeRingHom = ((↑) : _ → Completion _)` is `rfl` by the definition of `coeRingHom`, which is what carries `hψC`/`hψX` and line 129.
findings.issue: Three undocumented defeq bridges across the `RingHom.comp`/`Completion.coeRingHom` wrappers: line 122 offers `hψc.comp (Completion.continuous_coe _) : Continuous (⇑ψ ∘ (↑))` where `Continuous ⇑(ψ.comp Completion.coeRingHom)` is expected; lines 122–124 reuse `hψC`/`hψX`, stated about `ψ ↑(weightedC …)`, at `(ψ.comp Completion.coeRingHom) (weightedC …)`; line 129's `congrArg (fun g ↦ g f) key` crosses the same bridge back. Nothing in the proof records that these hold only by unfolding `RingHom.comp` and the `coeRingHom` structure projection.

summary: The uniqueness half of `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion` hides a reusable, strictly more general extensionality lemma inside the `∃!` proof, and it moves hypotheses across `RingHom.comp`/`coeRingHom` wrapper defeq three times with no lemma or comment. The rest of the file's proofs are short, robust, and free of `change`/`show`.
